A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Flowception and contain readable main text and Appendices A–H, including equations, proofs, tables and figures. Retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-to-video results on three datasets, insertion and attention ablations, qualitative interpolation results, and appendix experiments on length modeling and sampling efficiency.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds text-to-video comparisons, measured GPU sampling times, and qualitative long-video rollouts.

M1.justification: The original insertion/denoising framework and losses remain, but Appendix F adds a distinct inference extension beyond the context window. Algorithm 3 processes overlapping chunks, blends their updates and adjusts boundaries after insertions. Its parallel chunk updates conflict with the accompanying sequential-block description, leaving the exact implementation unclear.

E1.justification: v2 adds explicit text-conditioned video evaluation and generation beyond the training context window, including rollouts described as four times the training length. v1 already advertised text-to-video capability and proprietary general-domain training, but its reported evaluations did not demonstrate these scenarios. The public datasets and toy length-modeling task remain.

E2.justification: The new text-to-video comparison in v2 Table 2 evaluates original pretrained LTX and finetuned full-sequence LTX against Flowception. Existing image-to-video, autoregressive-attention and insertion-scheme comparator sets are unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 introduces evaluation using finetuned LTX-2B 0.9.5 with CFG 7 and 50 NFEs, a sampling-time sweep on one H200, and long rollouts at 24 FPS. Section 4.1 also changes the reported proprietary training-set size from approximately 20M to 2M videos. This is a substantial reported setting revision, although the PDFs do not establish whether it corrects documentation or reflects different training data.

E4.justification: v2 adds a wall-clock scaling analysis across sampling-step counts and qualitative case studies testing generation beyond the training context window. The existing insertion, guidance, causal-attention, local-attention, toy-length and FVD-versus-FLOPs analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run aggregates, confidence intervals or significance tests. Existing same-seed comparisons remain, and the added experiments do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation values remain unchanged. v2 Table 2 adds text-to-video results: Flowception improves five of six metrics over finetuned full-sequence LTX, including imaging quality 51.37 versus 47.96, but improves only imaging quality and aesthetics over original LTX. v2 also reports approximately 30% faster sampling and adds text-to-video and long-rollout examples. These are new results, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The probability paths, losses, insertion-hazard derivation, Bregman proposition and corollary, Poisson extension, and complexity formulas are retained. The added efficiency summary restates existing reasoning; no new theorem or proof accompanies chunked generation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the central claims about variable-length non-autoregressive generation, flexible conditioning, efficiency and generation quality. The introduction now includes text-to-video in its experimental summary, but that capability was already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: Appendix F newly identifies the main experiments as operating within the model context length and discusses longer-clip finetuning and overlapping conditioning as ways to extend long-horizon stability and continuity. The existing implicit-compression interpretation and doubled-iteration limitation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds code and project-site links, identifies the pretrained LTX checkpoint, and supplies Appendix C.2 instructions for framewise conditioning, padding masks and insertion-token placement. It also documents sampling hardware, example prompts and chunked-generation pseudocode. These substantially expand reproducibility information, although chunk parameters and the sequential-versus-parallel discrepancy remain unresolved.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds MAGI-1 by Teng et al. and Progressive Autoregressive Video Diffusion Models by Xie et al., distinguishing their left-to-right progression from Flowception's flexible insertion order. Other reference changes largely update publication metadata for existing works.

P1.justification: v2 makes local wording, spelling and citation-style corrections, updates author/contact information, and adds acknowledgements and targeted experimental and implementation subsections. Most existing prose and the overall section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual presentation with a text-to-video table, sampling-time plot, chunked-generation algorithm, and two new qualitative galleries. Figure 1 replaces two examples with text-to-video outputs and redesigns annotations and the color bar. Existing galleries are retained but sometimes resized or separated onto different pages.

improvement.justification: v1 advertised text-to-video capability and supported efficiency mainly through FLOP analysis; v2 adds an LTX comparison and measured GPU timings, strengthening empirical support. Adaptation instructions and code pointers also improve usability. The gains are limited by mixed performance against original LTX and inconsistent sequential-versus-parallel descriptions of the new chunked sampler, supporting a modest overall improvement.
